author: Pablo Halpern

evidence.note: Shows the author's original design direction and his later change of the container API from multi-function direct-return members to one optional-reference-returning member.
evidence.title: P3091R0: Better lookups for map and unordered_map
evidence.what_changed: R0 proposed `get` returning `mapped_type` by value plus `get_ref` (returning a common reference) and `get_as<R>` (returning a specified type) directly on map/unordered_map, avoiding optional. It explicitly considered, and initially rejected, the `optional<T&>` design because `value_or` would copy and because no `get_ref`/`get_as` equivalent existed. By R1/R2 and through R6, the author switched to a single `get` (renamed `lookup` in R6) returning `optional<mapped_type&>` / `optional<const mapped_type&>`, delegating the alternative-value functionality to `optional` observers and monadic operations.

evidence.note: Documents the committee-driven concession under which the author simplified the map interface and delegated alternative-value construction to optional.
evidence.title: P3091R2: Better lookups for map and unordered_map
evidence.what_changed: Records that after the 2024-02-27 LEWGI telecon (unanimous poll 6-4-0-0-0 for pursuing `get` returning `optional<T&>`), the author abandoned R0's `get`/`get_ref`/`get_as` API and moved the alternative-value functionality into enhanced `optional::value_or` (folded from a proposed `or_construct`). R2 also reflects LEWG's consensus that `value_or` returns an rvalue for both `optional<T>` and `optional<T&>`.

evidence.note: Pablo Halpern is a co-author and is quoted as preferring the name `lookup` among the proposed alternatives (try_at, lookup, try_lookup). The paper records criticism that the name `get` is inconsistent with other standard-library `get` functions and proposes replacing P3091's `get` with `lookup`. It also records a LEWG poll in Brno (0-8-8-4-4) that rejected extending `lookup` to random-access sequence containers.
evidence.title: P4139R3: We Need a Better Name for the Associative-Container Lookup Feature

position: Pablo Halpern has consistently and publicly argued that std::map, std::unordered_map, and std::flat_map should gain a member-function lookup that returns optional<T&> (optional<const T&> for const containers), so that key lookups can use optional's observers and monadic operations instead of find/end or operator[]. His original R0 design proposed get/get_ref/get_as returning values or references directly and initially rejected the optional return, but after the unanimous 2024-02-27 LEWGI poll he conceded and adopted the single optional-reference-returning design, first named `get` and later renamed `lookup`. He continued to defend the feature itself while accepting that the value_or enhancements he had coupled to it be split into P1255. Through his co-authorship of P4139R3 he endorsed `lookup` as his preferred name for the feature, though a poll to extend it to random-access sequence containers failed in LEWG.
recommendation: Proposes adding a `lookup` member function to `std::map`, `std::unordered_map`, and `std::flat_map` (in C++29) that returns `optional<T&>` (or `optional<const T&>` for const containers), allowing key lookups to use optional's observers and monadic operations such as `value_or` instead of `find`/`end` or `operator[]`.
title: Better Lookups for map , unordered_map , and flat_map
